title: The file is version 3 while its metadata table states Version 2
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx
section: Metadata table, Version and Date rows
description: The file name and the released family number say version 3, and the metadata table inside it says Version 2 with the date 15 November 2026. No source read for this document states which of the two is the current version, so the next version is numbered from the file family (version 4) and the source is read as version 3; the Version 2 row of the superseded file is left unchanged and recorded here.
evidence: File name: 'Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx'; converted text metadata table: '| Version | 2 |' and '| Date | 15 November 2026 |'; the same table names 'Document | Recovery Workbench cutover and go-live plan'. No other row explains the difference.
proposed: Correct the Version row of the source file, or record why the Version row lags the file name, so that the family number and the metadata agree in every later version.

title: Only the first release date is named; the Wave 2, 3 and 4 release dates and the wave to release mapping are not stated
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Section 1 How releases go live; section 9 Open decisions; section 10.1 Wave roster
description: Version 3 plans one monthly release and names the first release, 30 November 2026. Architecture v5 splits delivery into five waves and names no wave date, and no source read for this document says which monthly release carries Wave 2, Wave 3 or Wave 4. Version 4 therefore marks the Wave 1 release as 30 November 2026 (tentative) and writes the placeholder for the other three dates rather than inventing them.
evidence: Version 3 section 1: 'The first release, 30 November 2026, also starts the case list'; Architecture v5 slide 38 gives Wave 0 to Wave 4 and their services with no date; slide 38 note: 'BOT approval before Wave 1 go-live, if required (FPG 19/2560 cl. 5.5; up to 30 business days)'; the version 3 open decisions list DL34 (the release window) only.
proposed: Publish the release calendar with one date per wave, add it to DL34, and replace the placeholder of section 10.1 with the dates; keep every date marked tentative.

title: No source states that one wave goes live per release or how a wave maps to a release
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
description: Version 3 releases one deployable a month, so a release and a release scope are the same thing. The realignment has 19 services in four delivery waves and one platform wave, and no source read for this document states whether a wave is one release, whether two waves can share a release, or which services of a wave go live together. Version 4 assumes one wave per release and adds the cutover order inside a wave; both are recorded as assumptions.
evidence: Version 3 section 2 describes one deploy of 'the tag' per release; Architecture v5 slide 38 shows Wave 0 to Wave 4 with the service count per wave and no release number; Template and Rules R5.6 gives the business-epic wave map and no release identifier.
proposed: State one wave per release in the release calendar, together with the order of services inside a wave, and keep both under change control with DL34.

title: The first-release scope is written per capability, not per service, so the Wave 1 service that delivers each capability is not stated
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
description: Version 3 lists the first-release scope as case list, ACE views, spreadsheets, access, documents and tracker retirement, which are capabilities of one deployable. In the realignment each capability belongs to a named service, and the source gives no mapping. Version 4 adds the service to each row of section 7 and a services row naming the nine Wave 1 services, taken from the Ownership Map and the Architecture v5 contracts.
evidence: Version 3 section 7 rows: Case list, ACE views, Spreadsheets, Access, Documents; Architecture v5 slides 14 to 20 give the owner of each capability (case list in rwb-case, access in rwb-access, documents in rwb-document, notices in rwb-comms); Ownership Map v1 Services sheet gives the nine Wave 1 services.
proposed: Walk through the first-release scope with the nine Wave 1 service owners before the rehearsal, and record the owning service for each capability in section 7.

title: The rollback of version 3 switches one set of feature flags and redeploys one tag, and has no per-service rollback, no Worker Versioning statement and no rule package rollback
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1
description: Version 3 rolls back one deployable: flags off, then the previous tag, then the previous reference data. With 19 services a wave is 2 to 9 independent deployments with in-flight Temporal cases and versioned rule packages, and no source read states how a single service is rolled back without touching the rest of the wave, how an in-flight case keeps its build, or how a rule package is reverted. Version 4 writes the per-service rollback from the Temporal and Drools design and records the change here.
evidence: Version 3 section 4: 'Switch the feature flags for the release off', 'redeploy the previous tag', 'Reload the previous reference data versions'; Architecture v5 slide 23 rules: 'Kit versioned; workers pinned (Worker Versioning)' and 'Continue-As-New at stage ends'; Temporal and Drools design T4: rollback of a rule package is one call, with states ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED.
proposed: Add a per-service rollback rehearsal to the UAT rehearsal of every wave, and record the previous tag and the previous rule package version in the release checklist.

title: The BOT approval under FPG 19/2560 clause 5.5 is not in the cutover plan and its submission date is not stated
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Section 1; section 9 Open decisions; section 10.2 step 1
description: Architecture v5 states that a change of this kind may need a board-approved plan and prior BOT approval before Wave 1 go-live, with a decision inside 30 business days, and that the submission date belongs in the plan. Version 3 has no BOT row, no owner and no date, and no source read for this document gives the date. Version 4 adds the dependency to section 1 and to the open decisions, treats it as a gate on Wave 1 and leaves the date open.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 6: 'BOT may need to approve this change before go-live (FPG 19/2560 cl. 5.5, up to 30 business days): plan for it now'; slide 38: 'BOT approval before Wave 1 go-live, if required'; version 3 section 9 lists DL12, DL34 and DL43 only.
proposed: Confirm with Compliance whether the change is significant under clause 5.5, name the submission date and the owner, and record both in section 9 before the Wave 1 rehearsal.

title: Version 3 has the release read the 30 views under a recovery role, while Architecture v5 gives the views to rwb-source-data only, one login per service
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: Version 3 says the Workbench reads the 30 SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views and checks that 'the recovery role reads recovery.v_ace_* only'. Architecture v5 gives the views to rwb-source-data alone, with the login rwb_source_data, and every other service reads ACE data through that service's contract. Architecture v5 wins on source precedence, so version 4 keeps the 30 views and the 21 ACE tables and changes the login and the reader; the loser is recorded here.
evidence: Version 3 section 1: 'the release reads the 30 SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views (D-RCV-35, ADR-010)'; section 6: 'the recovery role reads recovery.v_ace_* only'; Architecture v5 slide 29: 'rwb-source-data, login rwb_source_data, recovery.v_ace_* views: SELECT only' and 'only rwb_source_data has SELECT on the views'.
proposed: Change the production grant to the rwb_source_data login, drop every other reader, and re-run the conformance test of the 80 appendix fields under that login before the Wave 1 rehearsal.

title: No source states the production capacity or the deployment slot model for a wave of up to nine services
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: Version 3 deploys one tag into one production slot. Wave 1 is nine services, each an api and a worker deployment, so a cutover night deploys 18 deployments and the cluster holds about 38 at rest. No source read for this document gives a production slot count, a per-service cluster request or a wave capacity check, so version 4 states the deployment per service and leaves the capacity position open rather than inventing a number.
evidence: Version 3 section 2: 'Deploy the tag to production in the change window', one row; Architecture v5 slide 8: '19 services in the rwb-recovery namespace, each an api and a worker deployment'; slide 49 note: 'about 38 small deployments at rest (most workers idle at minimum)'; no source read gives a production capacity figure.
proposed: Publish the production capacity and slot plan per wave with the cluster requests of each service, and add the capacity check to section 10.2 step 2 when it exists.

title: The tracker retirement names the six teams but no service, so the replacement case list per team is not stated
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
description: The tracker retirement procedure of version 3 is run by six team managers who work from 'the case list'. In the realignment the case list is the rwb-case screen, and the tracker data that no data product carries is picked up by a later epic. No source read for this document names the service that shows the replacement list per team or the extract the Tribe lead reads, so version 4 keeps the procedure word for word and names the Wave 1 case list only.
evidence: Version 3 section 8: 'Six teams own them: TDR, DIL, LIT, NPA, DEBT_SALE and WRITE_OFF' and step 1 'works from the case list'; Architecture v5 slide 3 and slide 14 give the case list to rwb-case (GET /cases, one case per case ID); the Ownership Map v1 Endpoints sheet gives no tracker row.
proposed: Name the screen or report each of the six teams uses in the retirement week, and record it in the six-team report filed on 26 November 2026.

title: The source carries no Status or approval row, and no approval of this version is recorded
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx
section: Metadata table; the document carries no approval or sign-off section
description: The metadata table of version 3 has five rows only, Document, Version, Date, Prepared by and Structure, and the document has no approval, sign-off or status statement. The realignment run takes no approval stop, so version 4 carries Status Draft and states that no approval is recorded; the open approval is carried here and in the assumption row.
evidence: Version 3 metadata table rows: Document, Version, Date, Prepared by, Structure; the document ends at section 9 Open decisions and contains no approval, sign-off or status statement.
proposed: Record the approval of version 4 by the release owner, the ACE team and the programme, with a date, and keep a Status row with the approver role in every later version.

title: The source carries no change log and no tool line
source: Recovery Workbench Cutover and Go Live Plan v3.docx
section: Section 11 Change log; the source has no change-log section
description: Version 3 has a metadata table only, with no change log, so there is no record of what changed between version 2 and version 3 and no tool line for the source. Version 4 adds the change-log table, records version 3 as the source row with the missing log as a gap, and gives its own row the D-RCV-60 change and the tool line.
evidence: The version 3 document has nine numbered sections and no change-log table, revision history or tool line; its metadata table names 'Prepared by | Henka Group' and 'Structure | Henka word rules' only.
proposed: Keep a change-log table in every later version and reconstruct the rows of versions 1 and 2 from the document properties and the release record.
